vignette: 55-year-old man with crushing central chest pain radiating to left arm for 45 minutes, diaphoresis, ECG shows ST elevation in V2-V4.
notes: Anterior STEMI. BA41.0 = Acute ST elevation myocardial infarction.

vignette: 62-year-old man, sudden onset epigastric pain and vomiting for 30 minutes, ECG shows ST elevation in leads II, III and aVF with reciprocal changes in I and aVL.
notes: Inferior STEMI, atypical epigastric presentation. BA41.0 = Acute ST elevation MI.

vignette: 68-year-old woman with 3-hour chest tightness, troponin I elevated at 2.1 ng/mL, ECG shows ST depression in V4-V6, no ST elevation.
notes: NSTEMI. BA41.1 = Acute non-ST elevation myocardial infarction.

vignette: 58-year-old man, new-onset angina at rest lasting 20 minutes, serial troponin normal, ECG shows T-wave inversion V4-V5.
notes: Unstable angina, rest pain, negative troponin. BA40.0 = Unstable angina (was incorrectly BA80.0Z).

vignette: 72-year-old man, recurrent chest pain at rest over 48h, troponin T 0.08 ng/mL, GRACE score 148, haemodynamically stable, ECG: ST depression 1mm V3-V5.
notes: High-risk NSTE-ACS, elevated GRACE, troponin rise. BA41.1 = NSTEMI.

vignette: 65-year-old woman with progressive dyspnoea over 2 weeks, orthopnoea, paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnoea, bilateral fine crackles, bilateral ankle oedema, S3 gallop, LVEF 25% on echocardiography.
notes: Acute decompensated HFrEF (LVEF<40%). BD11 = Left ventricular failure / BD10 = Congestive heart failure (ICD-11 has no HFrEF-specific code).

vignette: 74-year-old woman with exertional dyspnoea NYHA class III, preserved LVEF 58%, BNP 650 pg/mL, left atrial enlargement, diastolic dysfunction grade II on echo.
notes: HFpEF. ICD-11 has no preserved-EF-specific code; both BD10/BD11 route to the Heart Failure CPG.

vignette: 45-year-old man, BP 178/110 mmHg on two readings, mild headache, no papilloedema, no focal neurological signs, no haematuria, ECG normal.
notes: Stage 2 essential hypertension, no end-organ damage. BA00 = Essential hypertension.

vignette: 58-year-old man, BP 228/134 mmHg, confusion, progressive renal impairment (creatinine 280 umol/L from baseline 90), fundoscopy shows papilloedema and flame haemorrhages.
notes: Hypertensive emergency with end-organ damage. BA03 = Hypertensive crisis (was incorrectly BA04 = secondary hypertension).

vignette: 38-year-old man, LDL-C 6.8 mmol/L, Achilles tendon xanthomas, father had MI at age 42, Dutch Lipid Clinic Network score >8.
notes: Familial hypercholesterolaemia (definite FH). 5C80.0 = Hypercholesterolaemia.

vignette: 52-year-old woman with T2DM, LDL-C 3.2 mmol/L, TG 4.1 mmol/L, HDL-C 0.8 mmol/L, central obesity, metabolic syndrome.
notes: Mixed dyslipidaemia. 5C80.2 = Mixed hyperlipidaemia (was incorrectly 5C81 = hypolipoproteinaemia, i.e. LOW lipids).

vignette: 66-year-old man, 12-hour palpitations, ECG shows irregularly irregular rhythm with no identifiable P waves, HR 128 bpm, no structural heart disease on echo.
notes: New-onset paroxysmal AF. BC81.30 = Paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (was incorrectly BC81.0). AF CPG scope is the BC81.3 family.

vignette: 72-year-old woman, known AF, presents acutely with HR 148 bpm, BP 85/60 mmHg, severe dyspnoea, chest pain — haemodynamically unstable.
notes: AF with rapid ventricular response, haemodynamically unstable. BC81.3 = Atrial fibrillation (was incorrectly BC81.0).

vignette: 54-year-old man, 3-month history of exertional chest pressure relieved by rest and sublingual nitrate, positive treadmill stress test at 6 METs, serial troponin normal.
notes: Stable angina pectoris, classic exertional pattern. BA40.1 = Stable angina (was incorrectly BA80.0).

vignette: 61-year-old man, stable angina despite optimal medical therapy with beta-blocker and nitrate, coronary angiogram: 80% proximal LAD stenosis + 70% RCA stenosis, LVEF 55%.
notes: Multivessel CAD, revascularisation decision (Stable CAD / PCI). BA40.1 = Stable angina (was incorrectly BA80.0).

vignette: 34-year-old woman, unexplained progressive exertional dyspnoea over 6 months, right heart catheterization: mPAP 42 mmHg, PVR 6.5 WU, PAWP 10 mmHg, vasoreactivity test negative.
notes: Group 1 PAH, idiopathic, confirmed by RHC. BB01.0 = Pulmonary arterial hypertension.

vignette: 28-year-old woman, 2 weeks post-delivery, new onset dyspnoea NYHA III, echo: LVEF 22%, no prior cardiac history, no structural heart disease.
notes: Peripartum cardiomyopathy. JB44.3 = Cardiomyopathy in the puerperium (was incorrectly BD10.1, which does not exist in ICD-11).

vignette: 30-year-old woman, 20 weeks pregnant, known rheumatic mitral stenosis (valve area 1.0 cm²), NYHA class II, newly developed atrial fibrillation.
notes: Rheumatic mitral stenosis + new AF in pregnancy. BB60.0 = Rheumatic mitral valve stenosis, BC81.3 = AF (was incorrectly JA24 = pre-eclampsia).

vignette: 45-year-old man, 2-week fever, new pansystolic murmur at apex, 3 of 3 blood cultures positive for Streptococcus viridans, echo: 12mm vegetation on mitral valve posterior leaflet.
notes: Definite native-valve IE (Duke criteria). BB40 = Acute or subacute infectious endocarditis (was incorrectly CA40.0 = a pneumonia code).

vignette: 68-year-old man with bioprosthetic aortic valve, persistent Staph aureus bacteraemia, echo: perivalvular abscess, fever not resolving on IV antibiotics after 7 days.
notes: Prosthetic-valve IE with abscess (surgical indication). BB40 = infectious endocarditis; ICD-11 has no prosthetic-valve-specific subtype (was incorrectly CA40.1).

vignette: 48-year-old man, sudden right-sided weakness and facial droop, slurred speech for 90 minutes, NIHSS 16, CT brain: no haemorrhage, CTA: left M1 MCA occlusion.
notes: Acute anterior-circulation large-vessel occlusion. 8B11.51 = ischaemic stroke due to intracranial large-artery occlusion / 8B11 = Cerebral ischaemic stroke.

vignette: 65-year-old woman, sudden onset severe vertigo, diplopia, left-sided limb ataxia, MRI DWI: acute infarct in PICA territory.
notes: Posterior-circulation (PICA) ischaemic stroke. 8B11 = Cerebral ischaemic stroke.

vignette: 78-year-old woman, known AF not on anticoagulation, sudden left hemiplegia and hemisensory loss, CT: hyperdense right MCA sign, NIHSS 18.
notes: Cardioembolic stroke from AF. 8B11.20 = ischaemic stroke due to cardiac embolism, BC81.3 = AF (BC81.0 was incorrect). Both Stroke and AF CPGs relevant.

vignette: 52-year-old male smoker, T2DM 8 years, BP 148/92 mmHg on one agent, LDL-C 3.5 mmol/L, BMI 29, Framingham Risk Score 22% 10-year CVD risk.
notes: High CVD risk, primary prevention, multiple risk factors. BA00 hypertension, 5C80 dyslipidaemia, 5A11 T2DM.

vignette: 46-year-old woman, PCOS, premature menopause at age 42, BP 138/88 mmHg, LDL-C 3.2 mmol/L, strong family history of premature CVD, 10-year FRS 18%.
notes: CVD risk in women, female-specific risk factors (CVD Prevention in Women CPG). BA00 hypertension, 5C80 dyslipidaemia.

vignette: 42-year-old woman, 2cm firm irregular right breast lump for 3 months, mammogram BI-RADS 5, core needle biopsy: invasive ductal carcinoma, ER+/PR+/HER2-negative, grade 2.
notes: Early breast cancer, HR-positive HER2-negative. 2C61.0 = Invasive ductal carcinoma of breast.

vignette: 38-year-old woman, 5cm right breast mass fixed to skin, axillary lymphadenopathy, biopsy: invasive ductal carcinoma HER2-positive (IHC 3+), ER/PR negative, staging CT shows no metastasis.
notes: Locally advanced HER2-positive breast cancer. Histology is invasive ductal → 2C61.0 (was incorrectly 2C61.3 = mixed ductal/lobular).

vignette: 58-year-old man, 3-month altered bowel habit, PR bleeding, 8kg weight loss, colonoscopy: near-obstructing mass in sigmoid colon, biopsy: moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma.
notes: Sigmoid colon adenocarcinoma. 2B90 = Malignant neoplasms of colon.

vignette: 62-year-old man, tenesmus, fresh PR blood, feeling of incomplete evacuation, rigid sigmoidoscopy: mass 5cm from anal verge, biopsy: adenocarcinoma, MRI rectum: T3N1M0.
notes: Low rectal adenocarcinoma (T3N1). 2B92 = Malignant neoplasms of rectum (was incorrectly 2B91 = rectosigmoid junction).

vignette: 55-year-old man with lung cancer, constant chest wall pain 5/10, taking paracetamol 1g QID and ibuprofen 400mg TDS with no adequate relief.
notes: Moderate cancer pain, step-up needed. MG30.1 = Chronic cancer related pain (was incorrectly MG30.0 = chronic primary pain).

vignette: 64-year-old woman with advanced pancreatic cancer on modified-release morphine 60mg twice daily, experiencing 4 episodes of severe breakthrough pain (score 8/10) per day lasting 30-45 minutes.
notes: Severe breakthrough cancer pain on background opioid. MG30.1 = Chronic cancer related pain (was incorrectly MG30.0).

vignette: 35-year-old Chinese man, 3-month history of painless left neck mass 3cm, bilateral nasal obstruction, epistaxis, left-sided otalgia, EBV VCA IgA positive, nasopharyngeal biopsy: undifferentiated non-keratinising carcinoma.
notes: Nasopharyngeal carcinoma, EBV-associated. 2B6B = Malignant neoplasms of nasopharynx.

vignette: 72-year-old man scheduled for elective CABG, NYHA class III heart failure, LVEF 28%, T2DM, CKD stage 3 (eGFR 42), obese BMI 38, OSA on CPAP. Pre-anaesthetic risk stratification required.
notes: High-risk pre-anaesthetic assessment, multimorbid. BD10 HF, BA00 hypertension, 5A11 T2DM, GB61 CKD (all present in vignette).

vignette: 54-year-old man with T2DM 10 years, hypertension, IIEF-5 score 10 (moderate ED), testosterone levels normal, absence of nocturnal penile tumescence on RigiScan.
notes: Organic (vasculogenic) ED in DM/HTN, absent nocturnal tumescence → acquired, generalised. HA01.12 = Male erectile dysfunction, acquired, generalised (was incorrectly HA00.0 = hypoactive sexual desire).

vignette: 28-year-old man, ED present only in partnered situations but normal erections on masturbation and normal nocturnal tumescence, recent relationship conflict, anxiety symptoms.
notes: Psychogenic, situational ED with preserved nocturnal erections. HA01.13 = Male erectile dysfunction, acquired, situational (was incorrectly HA00.1).
